The main takeaway from our work is that

NGC 604, the supergiant star-forming region in the nearby spiral galaxy M33, has a rich structure of molecular gas, which is distributed in a ring-like structure with an inner diameter of about 100 pc.

NGC 604 is a very active star-forming region, with the most massive stars in the central region of NGC 604, and that the molecular gas is being compressed by the expanding ionizing radiation from the central OB cluster.
the H II region in NGC 604 has been expanding in a nearly isotropic manner for the past ~ 2 Myrs and has pushed the molecular gas outward.
